note: Candidate models for the Fanforge benchmark. Every entry is a local Ollama model; nothing here talks to a network service. 'key' is the stable name used in run directories and reports. 'seed' is fixed so the same prompt gives the same result where the runtime honours it. 'system' describes how the system prompt is delivered: 'separate' is the normal path, 'merged' folds the system prompt into the first user turn. 'think' turns the model's visible thinking off: gemma4 and ornith are thinking models, and with thinking on the answer comes out of the same token budget as the reasoning, which is not comparable with a model that does not think.

models.label: Qwen2.5 7B (baseline)
models.notes: The incumbent: the model the repository was built and measured against. Its chat template supports a system role, but the benchmark delivers the system prompt the same way to every candidate, so the framing is identical.

models.label: Qwen2.5 3B
models.notes: The cheap extraction model the README already recommends. Included to see whether a small model can do the indexing work.

models.label: Gemma 4 12B (Q4_K_M)
models.notes: Newer general-purpose candidate, 11.9B parameters at Q4_K_M. It is a thinking model, so the thinking is turned off: with it on, the answer comes out of the same budget as the reasoning.

models.label: Ornith 1.5 9B
models.notes: Nine-billion-parameter fiction-oriented candidate. It is a thinking model (thinking off) and it does not follow a system-role message: with the system prompt merged into the user turn it obeys it, with a separate system message it ignores it. That matters in production, where Fanforge sends a system message.

unavailable.label: BookBuilder Bookwriter v1
unavailable.unavailable: The upstream repository (Fordentinc/book-builder-bookwriter-v1, a Qwen2.5-7B prose fine-tune with GGUF weights) returns HTTP 401 for anonymous downloads, so it cannot be pulled into this environment without a Hugging Face token and acceptance of the repository terms. It was not evaluated.
unavailable.notes: Worth re-testing on a machine with the weights available, behind a prompt adapter, because the handoff expects a specialised writer to trade outline adherence for prose.
